mainTopic: Exchanging מעשר שני coins for gold, and whether a coin can take part in a חליפין transaction
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about exchanging silver מעשר שני coins for gold דינרים. One view says the argument is only a rabbinic גזירה, because a person might delay his trip to ירושלים. On that view, everyone allows produce onto דינרים, since produce rots. Another view says produce is also disputed. The גמרא shows that the משנה's wording, "יעשה / לא יעשה," fits a rabbinic גזירה, so the Torah-law version is left with a קשיא. Then a new topic begins: רב and לוי argue whether a coin can be used for חליפין, and רב פפא explains the view that it cannot, since a coin's value rests on a stamp that can be cancelled. The גמרא tests this against the rule "the gold acquires the silver," going back and forth over whether that case is a plain purchase (דמים) or an exchange (חליפין). רב אשי keeps the purchase reading, and רב פפא says a coin can be acquired through חליפין even if it cannot make one. A ברייתא about a man giving away his produce at the threshing floor begins a challenge to רב פפא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First view: a rabbinic worry about delaying the trip to Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: According to the first view, בית שמאי forbid exchanging silver for gold because of a rabbinic גזירה. They fear a person might delay going to ירושלים until he has enough silver for a full gold דינר. בית הלל do not make this גזירה. Everyone agrees produce may be redeemed onto דינרים, because produce rots and he won't hold onto it.
steps.simpleTranslation: [בית שמאי decree] lest he delay his trips up to ירושלים. Sometimes the silver coins don't add up to a full gold דינר, and he won't go up. בית הלל hold: we don't decree that he might delay his trips. Even when the coins don't add up to a דינר, he will surely bring them up. But with produce onto דינרים, everyone agrees we may redeem. Since produce rots, he won't hold onto it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of the first view of the בית שמאי / בית הלל dispute. On this view, the argument is only about a rabbinic worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the whole argument is a rabbinic גזירה, not Torah law. בית שמאי worry that someone with silver מעשר שני coins will wait until he can trade up to a full gold דינר, and so delay his trip. Produce is different, because it rots. Nobody would sit on rotting produce, so everyone agrees produce may be redeemed onto דינרים.

keyTerms.meaning: He will delay his trips up (to ירושלים)
We redeem / transfer the holiness onto something else

steps.confusionAlert: This text starts in the middle of a sentence. The words "lest he delay" give בית שמאי's reason, from the earlier part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: lest he delay his trips up to ירושלים,
phrases.notes: This is בית שמאי's worry, carried over from the end of the previous amud.

phrases.english: for sometimes they do not fill up
phrases.notes: Literally "fill"; he means the silver coins don't add up to the value of one gold דינר.

phrases.english: the silver coins to a gold dinar, and he will not go up.
And בית הלל hold:
we do not decree out of concern that he will delay his trips up,
for even when they don't add up to a dinar,
he will surely bring them up.
But with redeeming produce onto dinars,
everyone agrees that we may redeem,
because since the produce rots, he will not hold onto it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the first opinion begun before this text
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute over silver onto gold is a rabbinic גזירה about delaying the trip. Produce onto דינרים is permitted by all.

steps.title: Second view: the dispute covers produce too
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says that even redeeming produce onto gold דינרים is part of the dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: even with produce onto דינרים, there is also a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The second אמורא disagrees with the first. He says that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue even about produce onto דינרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view used the fact that produce rots to say everyone permits it. This view does not accept that. He holds that בית שמאי would worry about delay even with produce.

phrases.english: And one said:
even with redeeming produce onto dinars,
there is also a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּפֵירוֹת עַל דִּינָרִין נָמֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the limit set in step 1 about produce
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce onto דינרים is also disputed.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה fits a rabbinic decree, not Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses the words "יעשה" (he may do) and "לא יעשה" (he may not do). That wording fits a rabbinic גזירה, which deals with what you should do in the first place. If the argument were about Torah law, the משנה should have said "we redeem" or "we do not redeem."
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the version you said holds that by Torah law it is fully permitted and the rabbis decreed against it. That explains why the משנה says "he may do" and "he may not do." But the other version you said holds that they argue about Torah law. On that version, the משנה should have said "we redeem" and "we do not redeem"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the approach that says בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about Torah law. It uses the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "May / may not do" describes how a person should act from the start, which matches a rabbinic גזירה. If the argument were about Torah law, the question would be whether the redemption works at all. Then the משנה should have used the words "we redeem / we don't redeem."

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense according to...

phrases.english: Granted, according to that version which you said,
that by Torah law it is fully permitted,
and it is the rabbis who decreed against it,
that is why the משנה teaches
"he may do" and "he may not do."
phrases.notes: These are the words the משנה uses for בית הלל and בית שמאי.

phrases.english: But according to that version which you said,
that they argue about Torah law,
it should have said "we redeem" and "we do not redeem"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the different versions of the dispute and challenges one of them
steps.kashyaTarget: The version that says בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording "יעשה / לא יעשה" points to a rule about what to do in the first place, which fits a rabbinic גזירה. A Torah-law argument would be phrased as "מחללינן / לא מחללינן."

steps.title: The challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא does not answer the challenge. It stays a difficulty for the Torah-law version.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer. The Torah-law version is left with an unanswered difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "קשיא" means the question is not answered here. It does not mean the view is completely thrown out. The rabbinic-decree version fits the משנה's wording better.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult (the question stays unanswered)

steps.whatToRemember: The language "יעשה / לא יעשה" points to a rabbinic גזירה. That is why the Torah-law version of the בית שמאי / בית הלל dispute is left with a קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: A "קשיא" left like this is not the same as "תיובתא." The view is weakened, but it is not formally refuted.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 3 without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The Torah-law version stays difficult because of the משנה's wording.

steps.title: New topic: can a coin be used for חליפין?
steps.stepSummary: רב and לוי argue about this. One says a coin can serve as the object in a חליפין (exchange) transaction. The other says it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב and לוי. One said: a coin can be used for חליפין. And one said: a coin cannot be used for חליפין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It brings an argument between רב and לוי about using a coin in a חליפין transaction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליפין is a way of acquiring something by exchanging one item for another. The question is whether a coin can be the item handed over. The other option is that only real goods, like utensils or produce, can do this.

phrases.english: It was stated: רב and לוי.
One said: a coin can be used for exchange (חליפין),

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אֵין מַטְבֵּעַ נַעֲשֶׂה חֲלִיפִין.
phrases.english: and one said: a coin cannot be used for exchange.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about coins and acquisition
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether a coin can serve as the object of חליפין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute sets up the rest of the sugya about whether coins count as "money" or as goods when it comes to acquiring things.

steps.title: רב פפא explains: people value a coin for its stamp, which can be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains why someone would say a coin cannot be used for חליפין. A person values a coin because of its official stamp. That stamp can be cancelled by the government, so the coin's worth isn't solid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What is the reason of the one who says a coin cannot be used for חליפין? Because a person's mind is on the stamp, and the stamp is likely to be cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the reason behind the view that a coin cannot be used for חליפין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A coin is worth what it is because of the government's stamp, not because of its metal. Since the government can cancel the stamp, the coin is not a stable object of value. That makes it unfit to be the item handed over in a חליפין exchange.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind / what he cares about
The stamp or image on the coin

steps.whatToRemember: A coin's value depends on its government stamp, which can be cancelled. That is why one view holds a coin cannot be used for חליפין.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
What is the reason of the one who says
a coin cannot be used for exchange?
Because his mind is on the stamp,
phrases.notes: He means the person receiving the coin cares about the official image, not the metal itself.

phrases.english: and the stamp is likely to be cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of the second opinion in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coin cannot be used for חליפין because its value depends on a stamp that can be cancelled.

steps.title: A proof from the משנה that a coin can be used for exchange
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה 'the gold acquires the silver' to prove that a מטבע can be used for חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: the gold acquires the silver. Isn't that talking about an exchange? Then we learn that a coin can be used for חליפין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to settle the argument from Step 5 by bringing a proof from our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that when one side takes the gold coin, the other side acquires the silver coins. If that works through חליפין, then a coin (the gold or the silver) is serving as the object of an exchange. That would prove the view that a מטבע can be used for חליפין.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not...? (opens a suggested proof)
Can serve as the object in an exchange deal

phrases.english: We learned: the gold acquires the silver,
phrases.notes: When one person takes the gold coin into his possession, the other person gets the silver coins.

phrases.english: is it not talking about exchange?
So learn from it that a coin can be used for exchange?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the רב/לוי dispute from Step 5 against our משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a מטבע can be used for חליפין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: הזהב קונה את הכסף.

steps.title: No, the משנה is talking about a plain purchase
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The משנה could be talking about buying with money (דמים), not about exchange.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about a purchase with money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the משנה another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a purchase with money, the silver is the payment and the gold is the item being bought. Taking the gold finishes the sale. So the משנה does not need חליפין, and nothing is proven about coins.

keyTerms.meaning: Through money, a normal purchase where one side is payment

phrases.english: No, it is by means of money.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question about coins and חליפין stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be explained as a money purchase, so it does not have to involve חליפין.

steps.title: Then the משנה should have said the gold 'obligates'
steps.stepSummary: If it is a money purchase, the wording 'acquires the silver' does not fit. It should say the gold 'obligates' him to pay the silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'the gold acquires the silver'? It should have said 'obligates'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'purchase' reading from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a purchase, taking the item does not transfer the payment coins themselves. It only makes the buyer owe the money. So the word 'acquires' points to a direct transfer of the silver, which sounds like חליפין.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligates, creates a debt to pay

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי הַזָּהָב קוֹנֶה אֶת הַכֶּסֶף,
phrases.english: If so, why 'the gold acquires the silver'?
It should have said 'obligates'!
phrases.notes: Meaning: taking the gold makes the buyer owe the silver, but the silver coins are not his yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה as a money purchase (בדמים).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'acquires' does not match a purchase, where the payment is only owed.

steps.title: Read the משנה as 'the gold obligates'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing the wording of the משנה to 'the gold obligates.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it this way: the gold obligates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the 'purchase' reading by fixing the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the word 'obligates,' the משנה fits a money purchase perfectly. Taking the gold makes the buyer owe the silver.

phrases.english: Teach: the gold obligates.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Acquires' meant a direct transfer of the silver by חליפין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה should read 'obligates,' which describes a money purchase.

steps.title: The end of the משנה supports the 'purchase' reading
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says silver does not acquire gold. That fits a purchase, since a coin cannot buy a commodity by itself. With חליפין, each side should acquire from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense, since the end of the משנה says: the silver does not acquire the gold. If it is a purchase, that fits what we said: gold is a commodity, silver is a coin, and a coin does not acquire a commodity. But if it is exchange, each should acquire the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the 'purchase' reading using the last part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a purchase, only taking the item (the gold) completes the deal. Taking the payment (the silver) does nothing, which explains the סיפא. In חליפין, either side taking his object completes the whole deal, so the סיפא would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It also makes sense this way
The later part of a משנה or ברייתא
A commodity, an item being bought

phrases.english: So too it makes sense,
since the end of the Mishnah teaches:
the silver does not acquire the gold.
It works well if you say it is a purchase with money,
that is what we said: gold is a commodity,
and silver is currency,
and currency does not acquire a commodity.
But if you say it is by exchange,
let both acquire from each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support to the reading of Steps 8 and 10.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is talking about a money purchase, not חליפין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: הכסף אינו קונה את הזהב.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives a second support for the 'purchase' reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if someone sold silver coins for a gold coin, taking the silver does not finish the deal until the gold is taken. That fits a purchase, not חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, a ברייתא teaches: silver does not acquire gold. How so? If he sold him twenty-five silver דינרים for a gold דינר, even though he pulled the silver, the deal is not done until the gold is pulled. If it is a purchase, that is why it does not work. But if it is exchange, it should work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second support for the 'purchase' reading, this time from a ברייתא that spells out the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says clearly that pulling the silver alone does not complete the deal. In a purchase that makes sense, because the gold is the item and has to be taken. In חליפין, pulling either side would complete the whole deal.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulled into his possession (a way of acquiring)

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught in a Baraita:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֶּסֶף אֵינוֹ קוֹנֶה אֶת הַזָּהָב, כֵּיצַד?
phrases.english: the silver does not acquire the gold. How so?

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר לוֹ עֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה דִּינָר שֶׁל כֶּסֶף
phrases.english: If he sold him twenty-five silver dinars
for a gold dinar,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמָּשַׁךְ אֶת הַכֶּסֶף –
phrases.english: even though he pulled the silver,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא קָנָה עַד שֶׁיִּמְשׁוֹךְ אֶת הַזָּהָב.
phrases.english: he does not acquire until the gold is pulled.
It works well if you say it is a purchase with money,
that is why he does not acquire.
But if you say it is by exchange, let it be acquired!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, clearer support to the one in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That the case is a money purchase, not חליפין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining הכסף אינו קונה את הזהב.

steps.title: But the start of the same ברייתא sounds like more than a purchase
steps.stepSummary: If it is a purchase, look at the רישא of the ברייתא: once the gold is pulled, the silver is acquired wherever it is. That sounds like a real transfer, not just a debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what, is it a purchase with money? If so, look at the first part: the gold acquires the silver. How so? If he sold him a gold דינר for twenty-five silver דינרים, once he pulled the gold, the silver is acquired wherever it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns around and starts a challenge against the 'purchase' reading, using the first part of the same ברייתא. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a purchase, the payment coins only become owed. They do not move to the seller wherever they are. The ברייתא says the silver is 'acquired wherever it is,' which looks like a direct transfer, as in חליפין. This reopens the challenge to the purchase reading, this time from the ברייתא's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what then? (turns the argument around)
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Gold is the commodity and silver is the payment in both halves of the ברייתא. What changes is who pulls: in Step 12 the silver was pulled, and here the gold is pulled.

phrases.english: Rather, what? It is a purchase with money?
If so, say the first part:
the gold acquires the silver. How so?
If he sold him a gold dinar
for twenty-five silver dinars,
once he pulled the gold,
the silver is acquired wherever it is.
phrases.notes: The silver now belongs to the seller even though nobody touched it. That is stronger than just owing money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, בְּדָמִים? אִי הָכִי אֵימָא רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from supporting the 'purchase' reading to challenging it, using the same ברייתא as Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the case as a money purchase (בדמים).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the silver is truly acquired wherever it is, which does not fit a purchase where the payment is only owed.

steps.title: The wording 'acquired wherever it is' fits barter, not a purchase
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge from the ברייתא's רישא. The phrase 'the silver is acquired wherever it is' makes sense with חליפין. With a purchase, it should have said 'the man is obligated.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say this is חליפין, because that explains why it says 'the silver is acquired wherever it is.' But if you say it is a purchase, then instead of 'the silver is acquired wherever it is,' it should have said 'the man becomes obligated.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in step 13. It shows exactly which words of the ברייתא do not fit the purchase reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In חליפין, the moment one side takes his item, the other item really transfers, wherever it is. In a purchase, taking the gold only creates a debt, and the buyer can pay with any coins. So the words 'acquired wherever it is' sound like חליפין.

keyTerms.meaning: Barter, where each item acquires the other

phrases.english: It works well if you say it is through exchange,
that is why it teaches
"The silver is acquired wherever it is."
phrases.notes: This quotes the רישא of the ברייתא from step 13.

phrases.english: But if you say it is through money (a purchase),
then this phrase, "the silver is acquired wherever it is"...
It should have said "the man is obligated."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the deal is a purchase (דמים)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Acquired wherever it is' describes a real transfer, which is how חליפין works. A purchase would only create a debt.

steps.title: רב אשי: 'wherever it is' means 'exactly as promised'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי keeps the purchase reading. 'Wherever it is' means the silver must be given exactly as described, such as from the specific purse he named.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It really is a purchase. What does 'wherever it is' mean? It means 'as it is,' just as he told him. If he said, 'I will pay you from the new purse,' he cannot pay from the old purse, even though old coins are better. Why? Because the other one can say, 'I want them so I can age them myself.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge without giving up the purchase reading. He gives the words a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words do not mean the silver transfers by itself. They mean the buyer is held to the exact type of coins he promised. Even a 'better' substitute is not allowed, because the seller may have his own reason for wanting new coins.

keyTerms.meaning: To age them; to make them old

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not say the silver is acquired by itself. It is still a purchase. 'Wherever it is' only means the buyer must pay with the kind of coins he promised.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Really, it is through money (a purchase).
And what does "wherever it is" mean?
As it is, just as he told him.
If he said to him:
"I will pay you from the new purse,"
phrases.notes: He means a purse full of new coins.

phrases.aramaic: לָא מָצֵי יָהֵיב לֵיהּ מֵאַרְנָקִי יְשָׁנָה,
phrases.english: he cannot pay him from the old purse,
even though they (the old ones) are better than them.
What is the reason?
Because he can say to him:
"I want them so that I can age them."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new meaning to the words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Acquired wherever it is' means a real transfer, which points to חליפין
steps.terutzMaskana: It means 'exactly as described,' so the deal can still be a purchase
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, the deal is a purchase. 'Wherever it is' means the buyer must give the exact coins he promised.

steps.title: רב פפא: A coin cannot make a barter but can be acquired through one
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that even the opinion that a coin cannot work as חליפין only means it cannot be the item that makes the exchange. A coin can still be acquired through חליפין, like produce according to רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Even according to the one who says a coin cannot be used for חליפין, that only means it cannot make the exchange. But it can be acquired through exchange, just like produce according to רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a different way to read the case as חליפין. He separates making an exchange from being acquired through one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that a coin cannot take part in חליפין at all. רב פפא says a coin cannot be the thing you pull to complete the exchange. But when the other item (the gold) is pulled, the coin can pass to the other side through the exchange.

keyTerms.meaning: To make (to be the item that completes the exchange)

steps.whyThisMatters: This creates a new idea: being the tool of a חליפין and being acquired through it are two separate things. The next challenge from the ברייתא is aimed at this idea.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Even according to the one who says
a coin cannot be made into an exchange item,
that only means it cannot make the exchange,
but coins can be acquired through an exchange,
just like produce, according to Rav Nachman.
phrases.notes: רב נחמן holds that produce cannot be used to make an exchange. The next step spells out the comparison.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מַטְבֵּעַ נַעֲשֶׂה חֲלִיפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different approach from רב אשי. It supports reading the case as חליפין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the rule into two parts: making an exchange versus being acquired through one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a coin cannot be חליפין, it cannot take part in a barter at all
steps.terutzMaskana: A coin cannot make the exchange, but it can be acquired through one

steps.title: The comparison to produce explained
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the comparison. According to רב נחמן, produce cannot make an exchange but can be acquired through one. Coins are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at produce according to רב נחמן. Even though produce cannot make an exchange, it can be acquired through one. A coin is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the comparison to רב נחמן's view of produce supports רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן already accepts that something can be acquired through an exchange even if it cannot be used to make one. רב פפא applies that same rule to coins.

phrases.english: Produce according to Rav Nachman:
isn't it so that even though
it cannot make an exchange,
it can still be acquired through an exchange?
A coin, too, is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֵּירֵא לְרַב נַחְמָן, לָאו אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא עָבְדִי חֲלִיפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the comparison given in step 16
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that a coin can be acquired through חליפין
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, a coin cannot be the tool that makes a חליפין, but it can be acquired through one, just like produce according to רב נחמן.

steps.title: A challenge from a ברייתא about giving produce as a gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא to challenge רב פפא. It describes a man at the threshing floor with no money, who gives his produce to a friend as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: If someone was standing at the threshing floor and had no money with him, he says to his friend, 'This produce is given to you as a gift.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רב פפא. Here it only quotes the start of the ברייתא, and the challenge itself comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only have the case: a man with no money in hand gives his produce to a friend as a gift. The rest of the ברייתא, still to come, will show why this case is a problem for רב פפא.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If someone was standing at the threshing floor
and had no money in his hand,
he says to his friend:
"This produce
is hereby given to you as a gift,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to רב פפא's rule in steps 16 and 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that a coin can be acquired through חליפין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the setup of the ברייתא is quoted so far. The actual contradiction comes in the next lines.
